description: Potassium is a chemical element with symbol K and atomic number 19. It is a silvery white metal that is soft enough to easily cut with a knife and is one of the alkali metals with a single valence electron in its outer electron shell. In nature, potassium occurs only in ionic salts, and it is found dissolved in seawater and in many minerals such as orthoclase.
uses: Potassium ions are vital for the functioning of all living cells and are necessary for normal nerve transmission. Most industrial applications exploit the high solubility of potassium compounds in water, such as in saltwater soap, and potassium compounds account for 95% of global potassium chemical production through agricultural fertilizers to remediate soil depletion from crop production. Potassium compounds are also used in glass production, bleach, soap, and gunpowder production.
characteristics: Potassium metal reacts rapidly with atmospheric oxygen to form flaky white potassium peroxide within seconds, and it reacts vigorously with water generating sufficient heat to ignite hydrogen while burning with a lilac-colored flame. It is unreactive toward nitrogen and saturated hydrocarbons, readily dissolves in liquid ammonia, and has a low first ionization energy of 418.8 kJ/mol making it a strong reducing agent.
